1. For each resource, follow the instructions to patch the image and resolve this finding.

To resolve this finding for Kubernetes cluster pods:
1. Go to the [Kubernetes Engine Workloads](https://console.cloud.google.com/kubernetes/workload/overview) page.
1. You can either patch the vulnerable image or remove the deployment.
    1. To patch the vulnerable image, do the following:
       1. On the **Workloads** page, click the workload deployed with the vulnerable image to go to the **Deployment details** page.
       1. On the **Deployment details** page, click **Edit** to go to the **YAML** tab.
       1. In the YAML file, find the **image** property and update the value with a new image URL.
       1. Click **Save**. The vulnerable Docker image will be replaced with a new image.
    1. To remove the deployment, do the following:
       1. On the **Workloads** page, select the workload deployed with the vulnerable image.
       1. Click **Delete**.

To resolve this finding for Cloud Run services or revisions:
1. Go to the [Services](https://console.cloud.google.com/run) page in Cloud Run.
1. Click the service deployed with the vulnerable image version.
1. On the **Service details** page, go to the **Revisions** page.
1. Allocate traffic for a different revision deployed with a fixed image version. Make sure traffic is not allocated for the revision with the vulnerable image:
   1. Click **Edit & deploy new revision** to create a new revision with the fixed image version and select **Serve this revision immediately** to route all traffic to this revision.

   **OR**

   1. Click on **Manage traffic** under **Actions**, and route all traffic to new or existing revisions which use a fixed image version.
1.  Make sure the revision with the vulnerable image does not have any traffic.

To resolve this finding for Cloud Run jobs or executions:
1. Go to the [Jobs](https://console.cloud.google.com/run/jobs) page in Cloud Run.
1. Click the job deployed with the vulnerable image version. If the job is currently executing, cancel the execution from the **Actions** menu.
1. Click **View & edit job configuration**.
   1. If the image version is selected via image URL, update the job configuration with a fixed image version.
   1. If the image version is selected via tag, visit the [Artifact Registry](https://console.cloud.google.com/artifacts) page to build a fixed image version. [Learn more about how tags are used with images](https://cloud.google.com/artifact-registry/docs/container-concepts#tags).
1. The finding will be resolved if the Cloud Run job with the vulnerable image version isn't executed for 12 hours.

To resolve this finding for App Engine:
1. Go to the [Versions](https://console.cloud.google.com/appengine/versions) page in App Engine.
1. Review the **Traffic allocation** for the version you would like to remove. Make sure traffic is not allocated for this version.
1. Select **Service** which contains the version to remove.
1. Select the version you would like to remove.
1. Click **Delete**.

Security Fix(es): * kernel: openvswitch: defer tunnel netdev_put to RCU release (CVE-2026-31678) * kernel: xfrm: espintcp: do not reuse an in-progress partial send (CVE-2026-52935) * kernel: USB: serial: mxuport: fix memory corruption with small endpoint (CVE-2026-63899) * kernel: bridge: mcast: Fix a possible use-after-free when removing a bridge port (CVE-2026-64032) * kernel: tcp: fix stale per-CPU tcp_tw_isn leak enabling ISN prediction (CVE-2026-64024) * kernel: usb: typec: tcpm: bound altmode_desc[] per iteration in svdm_consume_modes() (CVE-2026-63962) * kernel: Bluetooth: hci_sync: Set HCI_CMD_DRAIN_WORKQUEUE during device close (CVE-2026-63974) * kernel: ipv4: raw: reject IP_HDRINCL packets with ihl < 5 (CVE-2026-64114) * kernel: ipv4: fib: free fib_alias with kfree_rcu() on insert error path (CVE-2026-64572) * kernel: Bluetooth: hci_sync: Fix advertising data UAFs (CVE-2026-74509) * kernel: Linux kernel: Denial of Service due to incorrect GSO state handling in network fragment reassembly (CVE-2026-80590) * kernel: smb: client: fix OOB read/write from unvalidated DataOffset in coalesce_t2() (CVE-2026-89633) * kernel: perf: Fix addr_filter_ranges lifetime (CVE-2026-93817) * kernel: kernel: strparser: use-after-free via msg_timer_work rearm after strp_done() cancellation () * kernel: exec: Cleanup POSIX timers right after de_thread() (CVE-2026-98260) * kernel: ipv4: validate checksum_start before completing checksum (CVE-2026-99999) Bug Fix(es) and Enhancement(s): * Batch: z-stream xfrm - rhel-9.8.z (NST-Core-26W38) (JIRA:RHEL-256697) For more details about the security issue(s), including the impact, a CVSS score, acknowledgments, and other related information, refer to the CVE page(s) listed in the References section.","count":203},{"value":"A malicious GOPROXY was previously capable of forging up to two sumdb tiles that allow for a requested module to bypass the GOSUMDB check and persist attacker-controlled module content to a local Go module cache.

This attack allows for a malicious GOPROXY to serve malicious module content that cannot be detected by evaluating the transparency log.

All tiles are now correctly verified against their parents.

In order to determine if you have been affected:

rm -r go.sum go.work.sum vendor/ && go mod tidy","count":60},{"value":"Handshake messages, such as KeyUpdate, are always considered as state-advancing, regardless of whether a handshake has been completed or not. As a result, a malicious client can keep sending KeyUpdate messages to force the server to keep performing key derivation operations indefinitely.","count":59},{"value":"The ToASCII and ToUnicode functions incorrectly accept Punycode-encoded labels that decode to an ASCII-only label. For example, ToUnicode("xn--example-.com") incorrectly returns the name "example.com" rather than an error.

This behavior can lead to privilege escalation in programs using the idna package. For example, a program which performs privilege checks on the ASCII hostname may reject "example.com" but permit "xn--example-.com". If that program subsequently converts the ASCII hostname to Unicode, it will inadvertently permits access to the Unicode name "example.com".","count":57},{"value":"A malicious GOSUMDB was capable of serving arbitrary module content not contained within the transparency log.

This attack allows for a coordinating GOPROXY and GOSUMDB to serve a client malicious module content that cannot be detected by evaluating the transparency log.

In order to determine if you have been affected:

rm -r go.sum go.work.sum vendor/ && go mod tidy","count":55}]
